summary: At step 12 the Wizard applies a wished bear trap while standing on stairs. C apply.c:doapply() calls use_trap(), whose On_stairs branch prints “You can’t set a trap on the stairs!”, resets trap setup, and returns. JS doapply() refuses BEARTRAP before that state check. This is the same whole apply.c trap-setting family already assigned to B11 for the higher-ranked floor case; it independently exercises the refusal branch and does not reach sit.c bear-trap behavior.

source.branch: The player is standing on stairs and selects a BEARTRAP from inventory through the apply command; doapply() dispatches to use_trap(), whose On_stairs test precedes setting a trap or installing an occupation.
callers: cmd.c binds a to doapply(); apply.c:doapply() dispatches BEARTRAP to use_trap().
js/cmd.js routes a to js/apply.js:doapply(), which currently throws for BEARTRAP before use_trap() can check the stairs.
dependencies: use_trap() calls reset_trapset() on the refusal path. The same selected source family and gt.trapinfo state contract are reserved by B11 for synthetic/v6/wizard-beartrap-sit-floor.
On_stairs() and stairway_at() supply the source distinction between ladder and stairs; preserve that branch without a session-specific condition.

evidence: Saved challenges/evaluations/20260926075422-v6.json at cd03ef328d8cf2c6ecdbfb47f4f6bd21f85c6c37 reports 17 remaining screens of 29 and first stop at segment 0 step 12, selecting object o for the apply command; js/apply.js refuses object type 244.

Independent C recording challenges/cases/v6/wizard-beartrap-sit.session.json shows the apply prompt at step 11 and “You can’t set a trap on the stairs!” at step 12. The same step has ordinary turn RNG after the refusal; it creates no trap and installs no occupation.

Upstream apply.c:4388–4393 dispatches BEARTRAP to use_trap(). In apply.c:2821–2862, use_trap() evaluates physical and terrain constraints in order, chooses “on the stairs” from On_stairs() and stairway_at(), calls reset_trapset(), and returns before ttyp or occupation setup.

This case shares B11’s doapply/use_trap/reset_trapset source and js/apply.js ownership; it supplies an independent branch observation while the higher-ranked floor case supplies occupation setup evidence.
